- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33) or volatile, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 1–2% per day post-spike.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, apply “mean reversion” rule: add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to catch upward momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.33), model often misses late-period rallies; increase forecast tail end by 0.5–1.5% to capture sentiment-driven surge.
